correctness.rationale: The full allowed class is parameterized exactly by b=1/(24d²) and d in [1/sqrt(12),1/2]. A Jordan-decomposition argument proves the BV operator norm equals the maximum one-sided distribution discrepancy (including chosen atom point values); direct atom evaluation yields max{b+d−1/2,1/2−b}. The inequality b>2(1/2−d) follows from a global cubic bound; two strictly opposite-monotonicity branches meet once at 12d²(1−d)=1, and both indicator witnesses attain the resulting d/2. Actual standalone code has executed and verified exact rational root brackets, moment normalizations, independent discrepancy jumps and concrete extremizers. Finite tests support rather than prove the universal claim.

value.rationale: Positive cubic-exact three-node symmetric quadrature is a classical naturally defined design problem. A sharp worst-case integration guarantee for nonsmooth pointwise BV data is a meaningful robustness criterion different from the conventional maximal polynomial-exactness criterion. The unique rule and sharp two-jump extremizer classification improve the exact Gauss sharp error 2/9 to d*/2, approximately 18.7%, while making explicit the necessary loss of fifth-degree exactness. No unmotivated parameter slice or purely computational value is claimed.
